benchmark-fractions.name: Fraction and decimal pairs
benchmark-fractions.rule: Learn the friendly pairs: 1/2 = 0.5, 1/4 = 0.25, 1/5 = 0.2, 1/8 = 0.125, 1/10 = 0.1. Then count them up: 3/4 is three quarters.

break-it-apart.name: Break it apart
break-it-apart.rule: Round one number to a friendly one, multiply, then fix the difference.

divide-by-5-25-50.name: Dividing by 5, 25, and 50
divide-by-5-25-50.rule: ÷5: double it, then ÷10. ÷25: times 4, then ÷100. ÷50: double it, then ÷100.

divide-by-decimals.name: Dividing by 0.5, 0.25, and 0.1
divide-by-decimals.rule: How many fit in 1? There are 2 halves, 4 quarters, 10 tenths in 1. So ÷0.5 is × 2, ÷0.25 is × 4, ÷0.1 is × 10.

divide-in-two-steps.name: Divide in two easy steps
divide-in-two-steps.rule: Split the divisor into two small numbers: ÷6 = ÷2 then ÷3. ÷12 = ÷3 then ÷4. ÷15 = ÷3 then ÷5.

divisibility-3-9.name: Divisibility by 3 and 9
divisibility-3-9.rule: Add the digits. If the sum is divisible by 3, so is the number. Same test for 9.
divisibility-3-9.example: 156 → 1 + 5 + 6 = 12, and 12 is divisible by 3, so 156 is too.

flip-and-cancel.name: Flip and cancel
flip-and-cancel.rule: Fraction ÷ fraction: keep the first, change ÷ to ×, flip the second. Cancel matching numbers before you multiply.

halve-halve.name: Halve, then halve again
halve-halve.rule: ÷4: cut it in half twice. ÷8: cut it in half three times.

how-many-fit.name: How many fit?
how-many-fit.rule: Dividing by a unit fraction asks 'how many pieces fit?' Dividing by 1/4 means times 4. Dividing by 1/8 means times 8.

integer-sign-rules.name: Integer sign rules
integer-sign-rules.rule: Multiply or divide the numbers, then pick the sign: same signs → positive, different signs → negative.

minutes-to-hours.name: Minutes as part of an hour
minutes-to-hours.rule: Put the minutes over 60 and simplify. 15 minutes = 15/60 = 1/4 hour.
minutes-to-hours.example: 30 min = 1/2 h     20 min = 1/3 h     6 min = 1/10 h

move-the-decimal.name: Move the decimal
move-the-decimal.rule: Times 10, 100, 1000: slide the decimal right one place per zero. Divide: slide it left.

times-one-and-a-half.name: Times 1.5, 2.5, and 0.5
times-one-and-a-half.rule: × 0.5 is half. × 1.5 is the number plus half of it. × 2.5 is double plus half.

3.1.title: Percent of a number
3.1.move: Percent means 'per 100'. Write the percent as a decimal, then multiply by the whole.
3.1.hook: Slide the point two places left.
3.1.trap: Stopping at the tax or tip when the question asks for the total, or moving the decimal point only one place.

why.goal: Find any percent of a number, including percents over 100, and use it for money situations.
why.supports_future: Discounts, tax, interest and percent change all build on finding a percent of an amount.
why.why_you_need_it: Percents are everywhere in real life: sale prices, tips, tax. Doing them in your head saves you from guessing.
why.real_life: A 15% tip, 8% sales tax, 20% off, or a score as a percent of the points possible.
why.building_block: Next lesson connects this to proportions so you can also find the percent or the whole.

3.2.title: Percent and proportion
3.2.move: Part over whole equals P over 100. Find what is missing, then solve.
3.2.hook: Part over whole equals P over 100.
3.2.trap: Putting the numbers in the wrong spots, or forgetting that the percent always sits over 100.

why.goal: Solve every kind of percent problem with one proportion: find the part, the percent or the whole.
why.supports_future: Percent change, similar figures and probability all reuse part-to-whole proportions.
why.why_you_need_it: Some questions give you the answer and ask for the percent or the starting amount. The proportion handles all three.
why.real_life: What percent of the games did the team win? A $30 item is 60% of the original price: what was the original?
why.building_block: This is the same proportion idea as Unit 2, with 100 on the bottom of one ratio.

percent-of.name: Percent of a number
percent-of.plain: Write the percent as a decimal, then multiply.

over-100.name: More than 100%
over-100.plain: 100% is the whole, so 150% of a number is more than the number.

tax-tip.name: Tax, tip and commission
tax-tip.plain: A percent of the price. Decide if you need the extra amount or the total.

percent-proportion.name: The percent proportion
percent-proportion.plain: Part over whole equals P over 100.

find-whole.name: Finding the whole
find-whole.plain: When you know the part and the percent, solve part/whole = P/100 for the whole.

proportion.name: Proportions
proportion.plain: Two equal ratios. Multiply both sides to solve.
